question: For a frozen forecast p from the complete conventional species, coordination and internal swap-barrier ensemble, does adding one draw of the previously learned four-symbol visible encoder improve prediction of the measured outward A fraction more than an ordinary four-symbol code? p is always available, not charged to H. This is an increment over one fixed predictor, not conditioning on the full physical microstate or all physical predictors.
scope: Archived L20 independent endpoints only. Secondary validation experiment, not a revision of the negative primary barrier-inclusive mechanism transfer. These populations have historical aggregate results and the full blend was historically selected on cold validation. No new lattice configurations, updates, dynamics, test access or beta index 6. No re-estimation on transfer.
geometry: Existing cage_baseline geometry/anchor schedule. V is the oriented 3x3x3 visible species cube. The three A indicators are at V[0] minus three positive lattice unit vectors, with two intervening layers from V. Use their count/3, not a joint three-site likelihood. The conventional offset may see the radius-two halo, which excludes all targets. The seed-11 learned teacher was trained on its own width-three one-buffer static shell objective, not on these labels.
teacher: Historical motif.teacher(v,11), fits/w3-b1-learned-s11, original category order/orientation. Posterior arm receives a single categorical sample in expectation: sum_h pi(h|V) log q(Y|p,h). The argmax arm is a distinct deterministic four-symbol encoder; ties first. No decoder receives soft probabilities or neural logits as continuous covariates. Four categories means at most two bits per draw; no claim that all arms transmit two bits.
design: Cold beta index 9: full HGB fitted to 7680 canonical training parents; all readout and quantile calibration uses only the remaining 2560 parents (64 fixed origins per parent); evaluate/select once on original 2048 cold validation parents (192 fixed origins). Compare all prespecified alternatives and freeze identities, weights, quantizer thresholds and comparisons before any transfer archive access. Score index 8 beta 2.711111111111 original validation only as designated warm transfer; index 0 validation only is a hot descriptive specificity check, not a second chance.
arms: All decoders have the same affine recalibration of logit(p) as nuisance terms, jointly fit per arm; offset-only has only those two coefficients. All four-class arms add exactly three sum-to-zero categorical logit contrasts, with no p-bin interactions. Hard ordinary codes: A bits at the negative/positive opposite corners, number of vacancies/A/B among the three inward neighbors of the target-facing negative corner, the same counts gated by A at that corner (otherwise zero), and quartiles of frozen p (cuts estimated on calibration only). Choose best of six four-level tripod formulas and strongest ordinary competitor by cold validation, with fixed list order for ties. p quartiles are a nonlinear-recalibration control, not a local observable. No supervised physical codebook tuning or expansion after inspection.
fit: Minimize marginal per-site Bernoulli negative log score averaged over codes and origins, using the exact fractional target. Offset parametrization logit(p) + a + b*(logit(p)-mean_cal_logit) + d_h, sum d_h=0. Fixed ridge 0.5e-5*(b^2+sum_h d_h^2); no intercept penalty. Offset-only is nested. Score without penalty. No class balancing or fitted temperature offsets.
selection: Use cold validation mean expected log score (higher better) to select once: best learned (posterior then hard for ties), best ordinary (two A bits, vacancy/A/B counts, then A-gated vacancy/A/B counts, then p quartiles), best code overall (ordinary before learned for ties). Always report all arms irrespective of sign. Gate 'any code helps' if best overall beats offset-only by at least delta on cold validation. Separate gate 'learned advantage' if selected learned beats both offset-only and the best ordinary by at least delta. Cold selection intervals are descriptive, not confirmatory. A closed gate never reopens, even if warm scores look favorable. Negative or closed-gate transfer is still reported quantitatively.
decision: Delta = 100 micro-nats per outward site, using the historical conventional ladder's absolute resolution. At index 8 require the one-sided 95% lower bound above delta on the cold-locked contrast (and planted-control pass). Distinguish any code helping vs an RSMI-specific advantage. For the latter require the selected learned code to clear offset-only and every prespecified ordinary comparator at transfer, not only the cold winner: an intersection-union claim. One-sided upper bound below delta on the locked contrast rules out a meaningful advantage for that fixed comparison; otherwise unresolved. Other contrasts including hot are descriptive. The two questions are reported separately; no omnibus familywise discovery claim.
uncertainty: Average the three marginal scores then all origins within each independent parent. Compare codes on identical parents/anchors; parent-paired Student intervals conditional on frozen estimators. Report two-sided 95%, one-sided 95% bounds, SE and approximate 80%-power one-sided minimum detectable increment (t_.95 + normal_.80)*SE above zero or above delta when testing delta. Not population refit or code-selection uncertainty. Do not call score gain conditional MI, estimate joint MI, infer dynamics, or claim universal optimality.
controls: With fixed p,Y, exchange entire H origin arrays between distinct parents in reproducibly randomized disjoint pairs, without refitting, and report matched vs shuffled gains and shuffled over offset with independent pairs as units. Separate planted calibration exercise on actual cold features only: hard teacher code labels a planted logit offset [-0.75,-0.25,+0.25,+0.75] around logit(p); draw three Bernoulli trials by a binomial count for each measured origin (not lattice configurations). Fit the same decoders on planted calibration responses, evaluate on independently seeded planted validation responses. Require hard over offset and matched over shuffled lower one-sided bounds above zero. Never mix planted responses with physics results.
operation: Run cold, publish the emitted cold-lock.json and cold parent-score NPZ with this implementation and design, then pass the published lock's SHA-256 to transfer. Never edit or replace a lock to change a prediction. cold reads only cold banks. transfer reads validation configurations via rate.source_rows(data,index,(1,)), uses the same anchor stream and cage_baseline.extract, evaluates probabilities(...)[full_member] on its private temporary bank, and never calls open_bank with a new cohort. Index 8's release filename, beta and hashes identify it; its producer receipt has a local index of 0.
